- Action items for Redwood: share our standard DPA, identify which SCC module we recommend for your flow, and confirm our SOC 2 status for procurement.
- Ask for Acme: confirm whether Acme will be the controller for chat transcripts (my understanding from call: yes), and who on your side will own the security questionnaire (you mentioned Jane).

Attachments I'm sending: DPA_template_Redwood.pdf (our standard DPA) and a short SCC guidance note. Also linking to the questionnaire you referenced — happy to own intake.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You review the DPA and return comments (if any) — target EOD Thu 10/22
2) We propose SCC module: Module Two (data processing + additional safeguards) — Rishi to confirm technical fit.
3) Kick off vendor security questionnaire — Jane to share latest PDF; we'll complete and return within 3 business days.

If that works I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up Thurs to align on any redlines.

Thanks,

Marissa / Lauren — quick tech/legal note to help answer Acme: 

- Recommended SCC module: Module Two (Processor) typically covers our standard relationship when the processor is operating services from EEA/US infra and uses subprocessors. However, if Acme requires Module Three because they anticipate subprocessors outside the EEA or additional transfer mechanisms, we can support Module Three too — it just requires a few extra clauses and a brief review cycle.
- Controller/Processor alignment: confirmed — Acme as controller, Redwood as processor. We'll add a controller/processor appendix to the DPA that spells out roles, data categories, retention, and subprocessors.
- SOC 2: Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II report for 2025-2026. We cannot share the full report publicly, but we can provide the AOC and a redacted copy under NDA. Procurement usually accepts the AOC + SOC 2 summary. I'll attach the AOC and a standard SOC 2 cover letter.

I'll prepare a short note comparing Module Two vs Module Three (1 page) and send it back today.

— Rishi
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
